kai: Heads-up — after the RBAC refactor landed in canary (rollout 2026-03-19 04:12 UTC) we saw a service account from workspace 'beta-42' access an admin-only endpoint on workspace 'alpha-7'. possible cross-workspace actor sideloading. attaching quick logs below.

sec-ops-bot: ALERT: unusual_admin_call detected — sa:svc-beta-42@appsvc, target: /admin/org-stats, auth: service-account, severity: high :rotating_light:

anika: which deploy/PR introduced the refactor? pinging @maria and @ben for context

ben: PR #1982 — renamed ResolveWorkspaceAlias -> ResolveWorkspace. main change was removing the org namespace param. quick repro steps: 1) create sa in beta-42 2) call admin endpoint with header X-Workspace-Alias: alpha-7 3) request succeeds (should 403)

kai: logs snippet (sanitized):
```
INFO 2026-03-19T04:18:09Z auth: allow sa=svc-beta-42 workspace_alias=alpha-7 endpoint=/admin/org-stats action=resolve_workspace( alpha-7 ) result=resolved(id=workspace-123)
```

ben: suspected root cause: alias resolver now uses a global map aliasToID without scoping by org. code excerpt: 
```go
func resolveWorkspace(alias string) string {
  return aliasToID[alias] // BUG: aliasToID is global across orgs, should be namespaced
}
```

maria: ugh. that explains it. Mitigation options: rollback the refactor in canary, add an emergency policy that denies cross-workspace service-account calls to admin endpoints, and rotate service account tokens for affected orgs. We should also revoke any temporary KMS unwrap permissions for the impacted service accounts until we confirm no secrets leaked.

alice: Can we quickly add a temporary check in the auth layer to enforce: request.actor.org == target_workspace.org ? e.g. deny unless actor_org == workspace_org || actor has role org-wide-admin. That'd be the fastest stopgap.

anika: agreed. I'll open an emergency PR to add that guard and a feature-flag gate: `rbac.strict_namespace_guard=true` so we can flip in prod if needed. Will also include an audit event for all admin calls for the last 24h.

ben: i'll collect a list of all service accounts that successfully called admin endpoints since 2026-03-18T00:00Z and dump to a secure s3 path. sample query I used: 
```
SELECT timestamp, sa, target_workspace FROM auth_logs
WHERE endpoint LIKE '/admin/%' AND outcome='allow' AND timestamp > '2026-03-18'
```

kai: we've already informed CS to message affected customers if we find any data access; security triage channel is prepped.

maria: action items: 1) anika - PR for strict_namespace_guard + canary rollback plan (ETA 30m) 2) ben - auth_logs export + list of affected SA (ETA 20m) 3) kai - coordinate with CS/legal for notifications (ETA 40m) 4) alice - temp KMS unwrap revoke script and key access review (ETA 25m).

sec-ops-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: incident/2026-03-19-alpha7-cross-actor (severity: high) — responders: @maria @kai @anika @ben @alice

anika: starting PR now. will post link when ready. trying to avoid a full rollback if we can patch quickly.

ben: PR link posted: https://git.redwood.company/p/rbac/merge_requests/2015 (hotfix branch: hotfix/namespace-guard). includes test that ensures resolveWorkspace takes orgID param.

kai: good work. keep log of all mitigation steps in the incident doc. we'll follow up with a postmortem focusing on how alias mappings are validated in unit/integration tests and whether KMS unwraps need extra guardrails. :thumbsup:
